title: Violation of the Constant Genetic Effect Assumption Can Result in Biased Estimates for Non-Linear Mendelian Randomization
population: UK Biobank participants previously analysed for 25-hydroxyvitamin D and all-cause mortality (Sofianopoulou et al., Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2021) and other exposures
funder: Stephen Burgess is supported by the Wellcome Trust (225790/Z/22/Z), the UK Research and Innovation Medical Research Council (MC_UU_00002/7) and the National Institute for Health Research Cambridge Biomedical Research Centre (BRC-1215-20014). No statement on the role of the funders was found.
authorConflicts: The author has no conflicts of interest to declare.
result: The effect of the 25-hydroxyvitamin D genetic score on 25-hydroxyvitamin D varied five-fold between the lowest and highest decile groups, violating the constant genetic effect assumption of the residual method. A protective effect of vitamin D on all-cause mortality in people with low vitamin D appeared with the residual method but not with the doubly ranked method, and was substantially attenuated with the residual method after log-transforming the exposure. The author regrets that a primary conclusion of the earlier analysis is likely to be misleading and states that this does not prove a null effect.
